tags: how to stop a dog pulling on the leash
script: Walking a dog that drags you down the street is exhausting, but pulling is learned behavior, which means it can be unlearned. Dogs pull because it works. Every time they pull and you follow, they learn that tension gets them where they want to go. Step one, change what works. The moment the leash goes tight, stop walking and stand still like a tree. When the leash loosens, even a little, say yes and move forward. Step two, reward the position you want. Keep treats at your side, and give one every few steps when your dog walks beside you on a loose leash. Step three, change direction. When your dog surges ahead, turn and walk the other way calmly, so they have to pay attention to you. Step four, start somewhere boring. Practice inside the house or in the yard before you try a busy street. Step five, stay consistent. If pulling sometimes works, your dog will keep trying. A comfortable harness can make walks easier, but it is the rules that change the behavior. With short daily practice, most dogs improve within a couple of weeks.
